correctness.rationale: The theorem is an all-q induction: the 4 initial and 8 recurring bit contexts each admit exactly two six-symbol greedy paths to the block extremum, every other local path ends at most two symbols before the next block boundary, and low previous paths cannot catch up. The local lemma is a finite complete 64-input enumeration per case, reproduced by embedded checker.py; the final suffix 01 provides both possible appended letters from any nonterminal endpoint, while the 2^q paths at the final endpoint give exactly 2^(q+1) absent words. Exact greedy automata were separately checked for all 2^(2q-1) skeleton assignments for q<=5 and paperfolding ranks 4..10. Unbounded quantification depends on the proved induction, not finite sampling.

value.rationale: The shortest-absent-subsequence count is a motivated natural language invariant, and a complete all-q law is proved for an exponential-size family of 16q-bit words with 2q-1 free bits. Its dyadic paperfolding corollary has subsequence universality 3/8 of length and exponentially many shortest missing strings. The result is structural: a strict six-letter greedy-barrier recurrence explains the invariant, and does not follow from routine substitution of a known generic formula.
